- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 10–15 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early or overshoot after sharp historical price spikes, then fail to correct downward.
- Model underestimates mean-reverting trends — fails to recognize that prices often return to prior 10–15 day averages after volatility.
- Forecast error is more pronounced in the middle-to-late portion of the 30d window, suggesting lag in adjusting to recent price momentum.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher values, particularly when historical prices are trending downward — underestimates the depth of the decline.
- Forecasts should be adjusted downward by 2–5% for periods with strong downward momentum in the last 7–10 days.
- When historical price is above 75, model tends to overreact — forecast should be capped at 75–78 to avoid overshoot.
- Model fails to capture short-term volatility clustering — underestimates sharp drops after spikes, especially in the 10–15 day window.
- Forecast should be smoothed with a 5-day moving average of true outcomes to reduce overreaction to recent spikes.
- When true outcome is below 65, model often underestimates the drop — should be adjusted downward by 3–7% for low-price regimes.
